**What I found:**
- The address `0x7d1e…33a5` isn't a normal wallet right now. It has an EIP-7702 delegation, which means someone signed an authorization that makes it run the code of contract `0x143b41298cb0a6a83b3ab532aaafbbae3078bc46`.

- The same contract also has owner-only functions that pull out ERC-20 tokens, NFTs and ETH, and run arbitrary calls from the account.
- This is how a "sweeper" drainer works. The attacker attaches this code to a wallet whose key they've stolen, so any ETH sent in for gas gets taken right away. The owner never gets to use it to move their assets out.

Your main wallet has 1 ETH, so the transfer would have gone through, and the 0.5 ETH would almost certainly have been lost.

**Before you do anything else:**
1. Did you knowingly set up an EIP-7702 delegation on that wallet, and do you recognize `0x99999ff4…9999`? If not, treat that wallet's private key or seed phrase as stolen.
